source.title: GloCTM: Cross-Lingual Topic Modeling via a Global Context Space
source.authors: Nguyen Tien Phat; Ngo Vu Minh; Linh Van Ngo; Nguyen Thi Ngoc Diep; Thien Huu Nguyen

record.tranche_reason: The study develops and evaluates cross-lingual topic modeling, but does not test whether independently trained network representations become more similar with scale, across seeds, or under the other listed versions. Its representation-alignment objective is a component of its topic-model method, not a test of the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports topic quality, classification, and LLM ratings of cross-lingual topic pairs. These are not measurements of distances between independently trained models' representations. CKA is used as a training loss aligning topic proportions with multilingual embeddings; the reported ablation evaluates downstream topic-model metrics, not representation convergence. Figure 6's topic-pair ratings are a related but different construct and are recorded under fits_no_version. Table 2, Table 3, and classification results do not measure any claim version.
record.test_reason: This is a cross-lingual topic-modeling paper. CKA appears only as a training loss that aligns topic proportions with multilingual PLM embeddings, citing Kornblith et al. It neither measures similarity between independently trained models nor cites or relies on the convergence claim. All results are topic quality, classification and LLM topic-pair ratings comparing GloCTM with baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that GloCTM's Polyglot Augmentation, shared decoder and KL and CKA alignment losses yield better topic coherence, diversity and cross-lingual classification than the baselines.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a cross-lingual topic model; it does not reproduce a method for testing representational convergence.
record.problems: The study does not evaluate model scale, capability, independent training seeds, or representation distances between models. Figure 6's numerical values are not available in the supplied text; its qualitative descriptions do not provide those values.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly measuring any listed claim version were reported. Topic-quality, classification, and ablation results in Table 2, Table 3, and Figure 5 were omitted because they do not measure representational convergence.

untested.parts: No scale or capability trend in cross-model representational similarity.
No vision-language models or image-caption pairs.
No comparison of representations across seeds. Five-seed means are only performance averages.
No mapping or stitching between independently trained models' representations.
No analysis of features or circuits recurring across models.
No test of how similarity measures or inputs affect measured convergence.
No measurement of how complete cross-model alignment is, or what causes it.

record.verdict_notes: The record's fits_no_version entry is removed. Topic-pair alignment from a topic model is not a related construct of model-representation convergence; it is simply the paper's own method performance. In the ablation, the CKA loss toward PLM embeddings improves downstream metrics slightly (EN-C 0.718 to 0.763). This is an engineered alignment objective, not convergence that arises on its own.

versions.untested_parts: Scale and capability trends in representational similarity between independently trained models.
Vision-language model representations of paired images and captions, and alignment trends as both models improve.
Feature or subspace convergence across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Mapping or interchangeability of representations between models, including linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Sensitivity of model-representation convergence to similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
Whether cross-model representation alignment is incomplete, plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.
